case.direction: I inherited the wordmark and the core colours. My job was everything around them: how the purple, the mint and the chevron behave across hundreds of assets in English and Arabic. Single campaign systems reached 80 assets across two languages and five formats.

title: AYWA
kind: Brand identity for a fintech app
line: An identity concept for a card and money app aimed at Egypt's 16 to 28 year olds. Aywa is the loud Egyptian yes.
meta: Wordmark, symbol, card design, app, campaign, out-of-home, social

case.year: TODO: year or years of the project
case.context: TODO: optional. Who the client is and the situation before you started.
case.challenge: A self-set brief: an identity for a Gen Z money app that feels as quick and direct as the product it imagines, with four minutes to open an account and one tap to pay, send or split a bill.
case.direction: The idea is money in colour. Your money splits into five pockets, and the colours from the photography become those pockets: pink for going out, volt for main, orange for food, blue for saving and chrome for bills. Each pocket gets its own virtual card, so you always see where your money goes.
case.system: In the concept, AYWA opens an account in four minutes with no branch, then lets you tap to pay, send in seconds and split a bill in one tap. The identity runs on one rule, the Lean: everything tilts 10° forward. The custom wordmark has no vertical strokes, and the centre of the W breaks the cap line by 18%. That peak becomes the app symbol and the hero of the card.

title: VULT
line: An Arabic identity concept for an energy drink named after a unit of voltage.
meta: Arabic wordmark, colour system, packaging, campaign posters, social, motion

video.caption: Brand in motion: the identity system animated.

case.year: TODO: year or years of the project
case.context: TODO: optional. Who the client is and the situation before you started.
case.challenge: A self-set brief: an energy drink identity that works first in Arabic and could only belong to this name, from the can to the poster to the feed.
case.direction: In Arabic, jahd (جهد) means both electrical voltage and human effort. VULT sits exactly between the two, and the whole identity is built on that coincidence.
case.system: Instead of a Latin wordmark with a gradient, the identity is built on an Arabic wordmark: four letters carried on a single wire, with a spark drawn into the lam. Six flat colours, no gradients, and a set of single-word Arabic headlines carry it from can to poster to the feed. The case study itself is written in Arabic, on purpose.

case.challenge: A self-set brief: a specialty coffee brand that feels calm and loud at once.
case.direction: The answer was a system of restraint. Three soft purples do the quiet work, ink carries the type, and lime appears once per composition, never twice.
case.system: The rounded wordmark hides a coffee bean inside the o, with three strokes of steam above it. An arcade pattern borrowed from the shopfront is built from one module and always rises from the bottom edge, across cups, pouches, bags, signage and the feed.
